tokenRules.message: Hex color hardcoded. Use semantic tokens (var(--primary), var(--bg-surface), var(--text-default), ...).
RGB/HSL hardcoded. Use semantic tokens via var(--*).
Tailwind palette color. Use semantic webkit tokens (var(--primary), var(--text-default), var(--bg-surface), ...).
Raw Tailwind text size. Use a generated typography class (text-heading-md, text-body-sm, text-button-lg, ...).
Legacy/external color utility. Use semantic webkit tokens (var(--text-default), var(--bg-surface), ...).

bounce.useWhen: Playful attention bounce (scroll-down hints); use sparingly.

brand-marquee.useWhen: A strip of logos looping forever (client trust strips, framework strips). Apply to a track holding its row exactly twice, the duplicate aria-hidden, and set animation-duration ON THE ELEMENT from the mark count so every strip on a site moves at one speed rather than one duration — a var in this shorthand would resolve at :root and never see it. Pause it on hover and focus-within so a linked mark can be reached.

content-enter.useWhen: Content settling INSIDE a page that is already on screen — a loading window resolving, a filtered list swapping, a step changing. Never on first paint of a page whose own entrance is already running (use it after that entrance, or after a wire). Stagger a follower with --content-enter-delay.

fade-in.useWhen: Content or backdrop appearing in place (no directional origin).

fade-out.useWhen: Content or backdrop leaving in place (pair of fade-in).

flow-dash.useWhen: Flowing connection along an SVG connector stroke in a node-based / network diagram. Set a stroke-dasharray whose cycle divides 24 (e.g. 4 4) so the loop is seamless.

highlight-fade.useWhen: Row/item briefly highlighted after an update (recently changed).

page-enter.useWhen: A page arriving on a route change — on the CONTENT ZONE only, never the shell. The chrome is the same before and after, and sliding it announces a reload that did not happen. Key it on the route path so a component serving several paths still replays it. Nothing inside the page may animate on mount at the same time: the two run in lockstep and read as one element travelling on a diagonal.

ping.useWhen: One-off attention ring radiating from a small element (notification dot).

popup-scale-in.useWhen: Anchored overlays opening (dropdown, popover, tooltip, menu); set --popup-origin.

progress-indeterminate-short.useWhen: Indeterminate linear progress bar (secondary short sweep).

pulse.useWhen: Skeleton/placeholder opacity pulse while content loads.

shimmer.useWhen: Skeleton shimmer sweep while content loads.

slide-down.useWhen: Vertical disclosure expanding (accordion panel, expandable row).

slide-in-left.useWhen: Left-anchored panel entering (sidebar, navigation drawer). Wrap the v-if region in a Vue Transition with enter-active-class.

slide-out-left.useWhen: Left-anchored panel leaving (pair of slide-in-left; use as leave-active-class).

texture-wave-a.useWhen: One of the two crossing bands of a pixelate texture, travelling left. Set --texture-wave-shift on the element to one period of its banding measured along X, and overhang the element by that much on the side it travels toward, or the field uncovers mid-cycle.

texture-wave-b.useWhen: The counter-travelling band of that pair (pair of texture-wave-a; same --texture-wave-shift contract, opposite direction).

props.concept: text of a link or call-to-action

events.noEchoRule: Do not emit "<x>-change" when "update:<x>" exists — it is redundant; use v-model / @update:<x>.

surfaces.product: Product UI (the console and other apps). The default for components.
surfaces.marketing: The marketing site (azion.com): page sections, bands, brand and client assets.
surfaces.docs: The documentation site: doc page chrome, callouts, steps, on-this-page.

props.name: singleLine
props.doc: Keeps the prefix unbroken and the label on one line while it fits; a longer label wraps instead of overflowing.

props.name: showCursor
props.doc: Shows a blinking terminal-style cursor after the label.

props.name: prefix
props.doc: Preset prefix rendered before the label; empty renders no prefix.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The label text, rendered uppercase in the brand primary color.

props.name: title
props.doc: The question, naming the action: ``Allow `npm test`?``, `Approve deployment to production?`. Backticks render as code.

props.name: description
props.doc: One or two sentences on what will happen and to what; backticks render as code.

props.name: state
props.doc: pending` asks; `approved`, `denied` and `expired` replace the buttons with the outcome in text.

props.name: kind
props.doc: danger` for an action that cannot be undone: the approve button turns destructive.

props.name: confirmationPhrase
props.doc: A word the reader must type before Approve enables, for irreversible actions (the resource name). Empty asks for no typing.

props.name: approveLabel
props.doc: Text of the approve button, the verb of the title (`Deploy`, `Delete`). Empty uses the locale catalog (`Approve`).

props.name: denyLabel
props.doc: Text of the deny button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Deny`).

props.name: loading
props.doc: A decision is being sent; both buttons are inert and Approve shows its loading state.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: What exactly will run: a `CodeBlock`, or `KeyValuePairs` with parameters.

props.name: label
props.doc: Visible loading text, `Generating <what>` or `Loading <what>`, with no end punctuation. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Generating a response`).

props.name: kind
props.doc: inline` pulses three dots beside the text (text responses); `bar` draws an indeterminate bar under it, where a table, list or code block is about to appear.

props.name: delay
props.doc: Milliseconds to wait before showing anything, so a fast response never flickers a loading state.

props.name: title
props.doc: File name or title of what was generated (`cache-rules.json`).

props.name: description
props.doc: One line on what it is or does.

props.name: meta
props.doc: Facts that help recognize it: size, rows, language (`2.4 KB · JSON`).

props.name: icon
props.doc: Icon class for the file type.

props.name: copyValue
props.doc: Text the Copy control puts on the clipboard. Empty hides Copy.

props.name: downloadHref
props.doc: URL of the file for the Download control. Empty hides Download.

props.name: openable
props.doc: Shows Open, which emits `open` so the owner shows the full artifact in a side panel or page (a canvas preview).

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The inline preview; scrolls inside a 20 rem body.

slots.name: actions
slots.notes: Extra icon actions, placed before Copy and Download.

props.name: from
props.doc: Who wrote the message: the person (`user`), the generative AI assistant, or the product (`system`).

props.name: author
props.doc: Author name shown over the message and read in its accessible name. Empty uses the locale catalog (`You`, `AI assistant`, `System`).

props.name: timestamp
props.doc: Time the message was sent, already formatted for display (`10:42`). Added to the accessible name.

props.name: state
props.doc: Lifecycle: `pending` shows the loading text, `streaming` marks the content busy, `complete` shows the actions, `error` shows the error line with Try again.

props.name: grouped
props.doc: Follows a message by the same author: drops the avatar and the author line so stacked messages read as one turn.

props.name: errorMessage
props.doc: Error text shown while `state` is `error`. Empty uses the locale catalog.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.doc: Loading text shown while `state` is `pending`. Empty uses `AiLoading`'s own (`Generating a response`).

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The content: text, `StreamingResponse`, `Reasoning`, `Sources`, artifacts. Not rendered while `pending`.

slots.name: avatar
slots.notes: Replaces the default avatar (person glyph for the user, the assistant mark for the AI).

slots.name: actions
slots.notes: Inline actions, usually `ChatMessage.Actions`; shown only when `state` is `complete`.

props.name: ariaLabel

props.name: minRows
props.doc: Rows shown while empty.

props.name: maxRows
props.doc: Rows the text area grows to before it scrolls.

props.name: state
props.doc: Request lifecycle: `submitted` and `streaming` swap Submit for Stop and block another submit; typing stays allowed.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables the text area, the submit control and every control in the slots' row.

props.name: streaming
props.doc: The model is still reasoning: the label reads `Thinking` and pulses; when it turns false the label shows how long it took.

props.name: duration
props.doc: Seconds the reasoning took, when the server reports it. Without it the component measures from `streaming` turning on to turning off.

props.name: open
props.doc: Controlled open state. Use with `v-model:open`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Initial open state when uncontrolled; collapsed is the default in a chat, where the response is the main content.

props.name: skippable
props.doc: Offers `Skip thinking` while streaming, for a model that can answer before it finishes reasoning.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The trace: short narration, steps, inline code. Kept as it was once thinking ends.

props.name: items
props.doc: The sources behind the response, in citation order; item `n` is what `[n]` points at.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: Id prefix of the list items (`<anchor>-source-<n>`); pass the same value to `StreamingResponse` so its citations link here.

props.name: title
props.doc: Heading of the disclosure. Empty uses the locale catalog (`3 sources`).

props.doc: Controlled open state. Use with `v-model:open`.

props.doc: The model's Markdown so far. Parsed into elements, never injected as HTML: raw tags render as text and only http(s), mailto, relative and hash links survive.

props.name: streaming
props.doc: Tokens are still arriving: shows the caret, marks the region busy and keeps an unclosed code fence as plain text until it closes.

props.doc: Sources the `[n]` citations in the content resolve against (title in the tooltip and the accessible name).

props.name: anchor

props.name: items
props.doc: Up to five prompts, most likely first.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the group. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Suggested prompts`).

props.name: orientation
props.doc: horizontal` wraps chips in a row (follow-up questions under a response); `vertical` stacks them (support prompts on an empty conversation).

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables every prompt, while a response is being generated.

props.name: name

props.doc: What the call does in the reader's words (`Listing your workloads`). Empty shows only the name.

props.doc: Controlled open state of the input and output details. Use with `v-model:open`.

slots.notes: What the tool returned, or the error it failed with.

props.name: model
props.doc: Actions rendered as rows in the attached overlay menu.

props.name: kind
props.doc: Visual variant applied to both joined segments.

props.name: size
props.doc: Size token; affects height, padding, and typography.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables both segments and prevents the menu from opening.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Shows a spinner on the primary button and takes the disabled status: both segments are disabled and the menu cannot open while it resolves.

props.name: updateLabelOnSelect
props.doc: When true, selecting a menu action updates the primary button's label and icon to mirror that action and marks it as selected in the menu. Opt-in; the mirrored action is also reported as the primary `click`'s second argument, so the consumer decides what each segment does.

events.name: click
events.notes: Fired by the primary command button on activation. `item` is the action currently mirrored on the primary segment when `updateLabelOnSelect` is on, otherwise `null`. Never fires while `disabled` or `loading`.

events.name: item-click
events.notes: Fired when a menu action is selected. `event` is the pointer/keyboard event that activated the option; `item` is the matched `model` entry. The menu cannot open while `disabled` or `loading`, so it never fires in those states.

props.name: series
props.doc: Series to plot. The first six take the fixed categorical slots in order; the rest fold into Other.

props.name: labels
props.doc: One category label per index: a string, a number, or a Date.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: Value axis direction. Horizontal lays categories down the side, for ordered bars.

props.name: labelScale
props.doc: How categories sit along their axis. `linear` places numeric or Date labels by value, for scatter plots and uneven time buckets.

props.name: min
props.doc: Floor of the value axis. Marks grow from one baseline.

props.name: max
props.doc: Ceiling of the value axis. When absent, the nice ceiling of the visible data.

props.name: cap
props.doc: Series kept before the rest fold into Other.

props.name: otherLabel
props.doc: Name of the folded series. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Other`).

props.name: formatValue
props.doc: Formats ticks, tooltip values and legend totals.

props.name: formatLabel
props.doc: Formats category labels on the axis and in the tooltip.

props.name: timeZone
props.doc: IANA time zone the default label format prints Date labels in. Empty prints UTC on the server and in the first client render, then the runtime's zone.

props.name: height
props.doc: Minimum plot height in pixels; the plot grows to fill a taller container.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Renders a Skeleton sized to the plot and suppresses interaction.

props.name: refetching
props.doc: Holds the previous render at reduced opacity while new data loads.

props.name: error
props.doc: Error message; when set, the plot renders a danger Alert instead of marks.

props.name: emptyTitle
props.doc: Title of the empty state shown when no series has a value. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No data available`).

props.name: emptyDescription
props.doc: Supporting line under the empty title: why the range is empty, or what to do next.

props.name: tableView
props.doc: Shows the data table in place of the marks. The table is always present for assistive tech.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the chart when it is not inside a ChartCard with a title.

events.name: point-click
events.notes: Click on the plot, or Enter / Space on the focused chart, at the active index. `point` carries the index, the label and every visible series value.

events.name: legend-toggle
events.notes: A legend entry toggled; `series` is the consumer's own series object.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The parts: Grid, Axis, Brush, Line, Area, Bar, Scatter, Crosshair, Tooltip, Legend, in paint order.

slots.name: empty
slots.notes: Replaces the default EmptyState.

slots.name: empty-actions
slots.notes: Actions under the default EmptyState, such as a Clear filters button or a setup link. Ignored when `empty` replaces it.

slots.name: error
slots.notes: Replaces the default danger Alert.

props.doc: Max height (CSS length). The viewport scrolls dynamically: horizontal scroll appears automatically when columns overflow the width; vertical scroll appears only when `maxHeight` is set smaller than the content (under the sticky header).

props.name: bordered

props.name: data
props.doc: Data-driven mode: row records.

props.name: columns
props.doc: Data-driven mode: column definitions (`{ id?, accessorKey?, header?, label?, enableSorting?, grow?, principal?, frozen?, width?, minWidth?, align?, kind?, resizable?, hideable?, orderable? }`; `width` (px) sets a fixed pixel column (also needed when a frozen column precedes another frozen column on the same edge, so sticky offsets can be summed); **`minWidth`** (px) sets a **floor** instead: the table measures the column's own content — its header, including the sort affordance, and every rendered body cell — and pins the column to the larger of the two, as **one** width applied to the header and every body cell (a per-cell `min-width` would let each row size to its own content and drift the header away from the body). It is for a column whose content is a chip or a short token: a fixed `width` there is a bet in both directions — too generous and it reserves space the rest of the row needs, too tight and the chip inside it truncates. The measured width tracks the **rendered page**, so a column can change width when paging or sorting brings longer content into view; `width` wins when both are set, and a user resize wins over both. a `grow` column without `width` keeps a shared fixed basis so the header and body stay aligned and the cell never wraps. A column with no `grow` defaults to weight `2` for the **principal** column and `1` for the rest, so the columns fill the available space proportionally. The principal column is the one flagged `principal: true`, or — when none is flagged — the first non-action column. A `kind: 'action'` column is automatically pinned to the trailing (right) edge — staying reachable while the rest scrolls horizontally — and is never resizable. **`resizable: true`** opts a column into a live mouse/touch drag-to-resize handle on its header (native pointer events; the `@tanstack/vue-table` exception covers sorting/pagination/selection/visibility, not sizing). On the first drag of any divider every flexible column freezes at its current rendered width; from then on dragging changes **only that column** and the table grows (horizontal scroll) — the others are untouched. The drag floor is the column's own content width (header label + visible body cells), so a column never shrinks past its content. Frozen and action columns ignore `resizable`. **`label`** overrides the `Table.ColumnSelector` label when `header` is not a string; **`hideable: false`** excludes the column from `Table.ColumnSelector` (e.g. the actions column); **`orderable: true`** opts the column into `columnOrder`. When non-empty, the table renders itself via TanStack.

props.doc: v-model:filters — structured applied conditions committed by `Table.Filter`, distinct from `globalFilter`. Client-side they map to TanStack column filters; under `manualFiltering` they are emitted for a server refetch.

props.name: filterFields
props.doc: Field catalog the built-in `Table.Filter` builder offers (id, label, value type, allowed operators, select options). Omit and use `Table.Filter`'s default slot to plug a custom builder.

props.name: state
props.doc: v-model:state — an aggregate serializable snapshot layered over the per-concern models. A bound per-concern v-model (e.g. `v-model:sorting`) wins over `state` for that concern.

props.name: initialState
props.doc: Uncontrolled seed applied once on mount; seeds only concerns that are not bound to their own v-model.

props.name: exportRows
props.doc: Rows `Table.Export` and `exportCsv()` write for the `filtered` and `all` scopes in place of the rows the table holds (the `page` scope always writes the rendered page). `useCollection` binds it so an export covers every match, not only the page; a promise is awaited before the `export` event and the download.

props.name: exportFilename
props.doc: Default filename for `Table.Export` and `exportCsv()` when no per-call filename is given.

props.name: stackable
props.doc: Data-driven mode: when the table's own box is narrower than `--container-lg`, each row renders as a card of label and value pairs instead of a horizontally scrolling grid. Set false to keep the grid at every width.

props.name: wrapLines
props.doc: Data-driven mode: cell text wraps onto several lines instead of truncating.

props.name: striped
props.doc: Data-driven mode: every other body row takes the raised surface.

props.name: density
props.doc: Row density: `compact` shrinks body rows and cell padding.

props.name: virtual
props.doc: Data-driven mode: render only the rows in view, for thousands of rows. The viewport scrolls vertically within `maxHeight` (40rem when empty). Ignored in the stacked layout.

props.name: estimateRowHeight
props.doc: Row height (px) assumed in `virtual` mode until a row is measured.

slots.notes: Data-driven mode: shown when there are no rows. Defaults to an empty-state block (illustration + title + description) following Figma; override the slot for custom copy/actions.

props.name: query
props.doc: The tokens and how they combine. Supports v-model:query.

props.name: properties
props.doc: Properties the suggestions offer, with their operators and values.

props.doc: Items that match the query, announced next to the tokens. Hidden when unset.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Placeholder of the field. Empty uses the locale catalog.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the field. Empty uses the locale catalog.

props.name: freeText
props.doc: Accepts typed text with no property as a free-text token.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables the field and the tokens.

props.name: mode
props.doc: tokens` turns each choice into a token; `query` edits one query string.

props.name: text
props.doc: The query string in query mode. Supports v-model:text.

props.name: validate
props.doc: Checks the query string in query mode: '' when valid, else the message shown under the field. Replaces the built-in check.

props.name: suggest
props.doc: Suggestions for the word at the caret in query mode. Replaces the built-in field, operator, value and AND / OR suggestions.

slots.notes: Composition slot; receives `<PickList.Source>`, `<PickList.Controls>`, and `<PickList.Target>` in flow order. The scope exposes the move actions plus selection/loading state, so a consumer can render custom controls inside the root in place of `<PickList.Controls>`.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: Bound pair of lists as `[sourceItems, targetItems]` (v-model).

props.name: dataKey
props.doc: Item field used as each row's render key (falls back to the index). Selection is always tracked by index.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables all selection and move controls and applies disabled tokens.

props.name: moveOnDoubleClick
props.doc: When true, double-clicking an item moves it to the opposite list. Set false to keep `item-double-click` firing without the move.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.notes: v-model update with the new `[sourceItems, targetItems]` pair.

events.name: move
events.notes: Fired after items move between lists, with the moved items.

events.name: item-double-click
events.payload: (event: MouseEvent, payload: { list: 'source' | 'target'; item: unknown; index: number })
events.notes: Fired when an option is double-clicked. `event` is the dblclick; `payload` carries the item, its index, and which list it was in. Fires regardless of `moveOnDoubleClick`, but not while the component is disabled or a list is loading.

slots.name: default
slots.scope: { move, moveAll, hasSelection, count, disabled, loading }
slots.notes: Composition slot; receives `<PickList.Source>`, `<PickList.Controls>`, and `<PickList.Target>` in flow order. The scope exposes the move actions plus selection/loading state, so a consumer can render custom controls inside the root in place of `<PickList.Controls>`.

props.name: items
props.doc: Nodes to render; each is `{ id: string; label: string; icon?: string; description?: string; disabled?: boolean; children?: TreeItem[] }`. A node with a non-empty `children` array is a parent.

props.name: selectable
props.doc: Enables single selection: activating a node writes its id to `v-model:selected` and marks it `aria-selected`.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Renders Skeleton rows in place of the tree and sets `aria-busy`.

props.name: emptyTitle
props.doc: Title of the default empty state shown when `items` is empty. Empty uses the locale catalog (`No items`).

props.name: emptyDescription
props.doc: Supporting line under the empty title.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the tree.

events.name: item-click
events.notes: A node activated: click on its row, or Enter / Space on the focused node. `item` is the consumer's own node object. Fires after `update:selected` when `selectable`. Not fired for a `disabled` node, nor for a click on the chevron or inside the `actions` region.

slots.name: item
slots.scope: { item: TreeItem; level: number; expanded: boolean }
slots.notes: Replaces the label region of every row (glyph + label + description). The fallback inside the slot renders `item.icon`, `item.label` and `item.description`. `level` is 1 for top-level nodes; `expanded` is false for leaves. The chevron, indentation, row states and the `actions` region stay owned by the tree.

slots.name: actions
slots.notes: Trailing per-row controls, end-aligned in the row (e.g. an `IconButton` that opens a `dropdown`). Clicks and keys inside it do not activate the row nor move tree focus. No fallback; when unused, the region is not rendered.

slots.name: empty
slots.notes: Replaces the default empty state. The fallback inside the slot is `EmptyState` titled by `emptyTitle` with `emptyDescription`.

props.name: kind
props.doc: Which admonition this is; drives the severity color and the icon.

props.name: label
props.doc: Fallback copy when the default slot is empty.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The callout copy: prose with links and inline code, or paragraphs and a list, laid out by the callout since `DocProse` stops at its edge. The copy region is a flow container, so server-rendered block markup stays inside the box.

props.name: lastUpdated

slots.name: action

The copy region is a flow container (a `div`, not a `p`), so block markup arriving from a server render stays inside it instead of being closed out beside the copy. Falls back to `label` when empty.

props.name: title
props.doc: Primary heading announcing the empty resource.

props.name: description

props.name: icon
props.doc: PrimeIcons/Azion icon class for the standardized adornment (e.g. `pi pi-inbox`). When set, renders a size-scaled featured-icon tile; when empty and the `icon` slot is unused, no adornment renders.

props.name: size
props.doc: Size token (subset — only `small` and `medium`; no `large`). Scales the whole block on one harmonic ramp — the adornment size, the title and description typography, the surrounding padding, and the gaps between adornment, text, and actions all step up together.

props.name: bordered
props.doc: When true, wraps the content in a dashed-bordered surface card; otherwise renders on a transparent background.

slots.name: icon
slots.notes: Custom adornment centered above the title, rendered inside an `aria-hidden` container. Overrides the `icon` prop's featured-icon tile. When neither this slot nor the `icon` prop is provided, no adornment renders.

slots.name: actions
slots.notes: Action area below the description; consumer composes buttons and the documentation link.

props.name: description

props.name: retryLabel
props.doc: Label of the built-in Retry action. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Try again`).

props.name: resetKey
props.doc: When this value changes while the fallback shows, the region is mounted again (pass the route path or the record id).

props.name: propagate
props.doc: When true, the error keeps travelling to the parent boundaries and the app error handler after this boundary handles it.

events.name: error
events.notes: Fires once per failure with `{ error, info }`: what was thrown and Vue's description of where. Report it from here.

events.name: retry
events.notes: Fires when the region is mounted again (Retry, the slot's `retry`, or a `resetKey` change). Reset the broken state here.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The region the boundary guards. Mounted again, from scratch, on every retry.

slots.name: fallback

props.name: max

props.doc: Show an always-visible close control on every toast; a per-toast `closable` option overrides it.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: Optional override for a single toast's body. `toast` is the store entry (`{ id, type, message, description?, action?, actions?, duration }`); `dismiss` dismisses that entry. When omitted, the `Toaster` composes `ToastItem` + `Title`/`Description`/`Action`/`Close` from the entry, rendering one `Action` per entry of `actions` (the first two) or the single `action`.

toast.setup: One-time app-level wiring before the first toast() call — service (recommended): import { ToastPlugin } from '@aziontech/webkit/toast' and chain .use(ToastPlugin) onto createApp() in the app entry; the plugin mounts the toast region automatically. Alternative: mount a Toaster component once near the app root. `webkit doctor` flags toast usage with no wired region.

events.name: navigate
events.notes: A leaf row — or the **label** of a row that owns children, of either kind, since such a row is a destination as well as a container — was activated in data-driven mode; `node` is the activated tree node. A row's **arrow** does not emit it: revealing children is a move inside the menu, not a navigation. A node with nothing to point at gives the consumer nothing to route to, which is the consumer's own check.

events.name: update:path
events.notes: v-model:path` — the drill stack as ancestor node ids, outermost first. Empty at the root level. **Persist it when the host remounts** (and always when a drill row navigates, which remounts the shell in most routers) or the level closes on the very navigation that opened it. A stack supplied this way is restored **with its label, its trigger, and its entrance**: every drill sub announces the first two to the root when its trigger mounts (not only when pushed), so the restored level still names itself in the a11y tree, `Menu.Back` can still name it as a destination from a deeper level, and popping still returns focus to the row that owns it; and the level _arrives_ rather than simply being there — see the restored-level row in Motion.

events.name: update:expanded
events.notes: v-model:expanded` — ids of the inline subs currently open. Persist it when the host remounts, or expansion resets and one sub appearing to close another.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The composed anatomy. Rendered **before** the `groups` tree, not instead of it — so a `Menu.Back` can accompany a data-driven menu, which is the one row `groups` cannot express (a drilled level would otherwise have no pointer route back).

headers/auth-header.name: AuthHeader
headers/auth-header.title: Templates/Headers/AuthHeader
headers/auth-header.summary: The console bar for the signed-out and onboarding screens: sign in, sign up, password recovery and the first-run steps. A `GlobalHeader` in its default `content` placement with the brand at the start and one outlined Documentation button at the end. There is no navigation, no search and no account control, because there is no session to act on yet. Built from `GlobalHeader`, `Button` and `Brand`.
headers/auth-header.guidelinesSummary: The top bar of every signed-out and first-run screen: sign in, sign up, password recovery and the onboarding steps. The user has no session yet, so the bar has one job: say where they are (Azion) and offer the one way out that needs no account, the documentation. Everything a signed-in bar carries (navigation, search, Create, the account avatar) is left out because there is nothing to act on.

headers/creation-header.name: CreationHeader
headers/creation-header.title: Templates/Headers/CreationHeader
headers/creation-header.summary: The console bar for the focused creation shell: create, edit and deploy flows that run without the navigation rail. A `GlobalHeader` in its default `content` placement, spanning the whole window. Start: a small back button, the brand and the breadcrumb of where the flow lives. End: the account avatar alone, so the signed-in user stays visible. The bar carries no search, Create or Agent: the flow is the one thing on screen. Every one-screen create page (SinglePageCreate), every stepped one (MultipageCreate), the creation wizards (SourceWizard, ProvisionWizard), the deploy flows and the CreateHub render it. The back button returns to the list the flow started from; the wizards drop it and the crumb once they reach the provisioning and success screens. Built from `GlobalHeader`, `Breadcrumb`, `IconButton`, `Avatar` and `Brand`.
headers/creation-header.guidelinesSummary: The top bar of the focused creation shell: create, edit and deploy flows that run without the navigation rail. platform/ai/ai-action-approval.name: AiActionApproval
platform/ai/ai-action-approval.title: Templates/Platform/AI/AiActionApproval
platform/ai/ai-action-approval.summary: A user-authorized action inside a generative AI conversation: the reader asks the assistant to deploy, the assistant records the read-only call it made (`ToolCall`), explains in `StreamingResponse` and proposes the deployment as an `ActionConfirmation` card whose title names the command in code, whose body shows the exact command in a `CodeBlock`, and whose Deny and Deploy buttons decide. Approving turns the card into Approved and adds a running `ToolCall` that completes, followed by a `ChatMessage` that reports what changed with Copy (`CopyButton`); denying or letting the request expire records the outcome on the card and the assistant says nothing ran. The `PromptInput` shows Stop while the approved action runs. Built from `Conversation`, `ChatMessage`, `ToolCall`, `StreamingResponse`, `ActionConfirmation`, `CodeBlock`, `CopyButton` and `PromptInput`.
platform/ai/ai-action-approval.guidelinesSummary: The moment an assistant needs permission. The reader asked for something that changes their account — a deployment, a purge, a deletion — and the assistant stops before doing it: it says what it found, shows exactly what will run, and waits for Approve or Deny. The decision stays in the thread as text, and the assistant reports what happened next, so the conversation is also the record of what ran and who allowed it.

variants.name: Irreversible
variants.summary: The assistant proposes deleting a domain nobody uses: the card turns danger and Delete stays disabled until the reader types the domain name.

variants.name: Approved
variants.summary: After Deploy: the card reads Approved, the deployment call completed, and the assistant reports the new build is live with the previous one kept for rollback.

variants.name: Denied
variants.summary: After Deny: the card reads Denied, the deployment call is recorded as denied, and the assistant acknowledges that nothing was deployed.

variants.name: Expired
variants.summary: Nobody decided in time: the card reads Request expired and the assistant says nothing was deployed.

platform/ai/ai-chat.name: AiChat
platform/ai/ai-chat.title: Templates/Platform/AI/AiChat
platform/ai/ai-chat.summary: The full-page generative AI assistant: a header with the assistant's name, a Preview `Tag` and New chat; before the first message an `EmptyState` that says what the assistant knows, over vertical support prompts from `SuggestionGroup`; then a `Conversation` where the reader's prompts sit at the inline end and each response is a `ChatMessage` that goes pending (loading text), thinking (`Reasoning`), streaming (`StreamingResponse` with numbered citations) and complete (collapsed `Sources`, Copy, Regenerate and the feedback thumbs), followed by follow-up questions; a `PromptInput` pinned under the log with a 4,000-character limit, Stop while a response is generated, and the disclaimer under it. The primary state is the empty assistant; sending a support prompt runs the whole response cycle. Built from `ChatMessage`, `Conversation`, `PromptInput`, `StreamingResponse`, `Reasoning`, `Sources`, `SuggestionGroup`, `EmptyState`, `Tag`, `Button`, `IconButton` and `CopyButton`.
platform/ai/ai-chat.guidelinesSummary: A full page where a person talks with the generative AI assistant about their account: they ask in their own words, watch the response arrive, check where it came from, and keep going with a follow-up or a new question. The page is the conversation; everything else (header, composer) stays still while only the log scrolls. Use it as the assistant's home; on a resource page, open the same conversation in a drawer with `platform/ai/ai-chat-drawer`.

variants.name: Streaming
variants.summary: A response arriving: the reader asked why storefront returns 502 errors and the answer streams in with its caret, a table on the way, the region busy and Stop in the composer; when it ends the sources, actions and follow-up questions appear.

variants.name: Error
variants.summary: A response that failed mid-stream: the partial text stays, the error line says the connection was interrupted and Try again regenerates the response in place.

variants.name: LongThread
variants.summary: Six earlier turns about one workload that overflow the log: it opens on the newest response, stops following when the reader scrolls up, and Scroll to the latest message brings them back; follow-up questions close the thread.

platform/auth.name: Auth
platform/auth.title: Templates/Platform/Auth
platform/auth.summary: The signed-out screens of a platform app, frame included: a full-height page with the signed-out `GlobalHeader` (the product mark and a Documentation button) over a centred column that holds one `Card` and the prompt and terms under it. It serves /login, /signup and /signup/verify. The Google and GitHub buttons lead the card, over an “or” `Separator`. Each field is a required `Label` over `Input` or a `Field` with `PasswordInput` and `PasswordRequirements`; a `HelperText` appears only after the primary action, saying whether the field is empty or malformed. The rest is `Button`, `IconButton` in a `Tooltip`, a `Tag` and a `Alert`. Errors follow one rule: auth never toasts. Each error story is one endpoint response, and every outcome lands in the same small `Alert` at the top of the card, above the fields. What changes is the severity and what it carries: nothing after a 401, because the fields under it are the recovery; Retry when nobody can fix it (503, 500, timeout); the Sign in and reset-your-password links when the address is already registered (409). Built from `PageHeader`, `GlobalHeader`, `Tag`, `Card`, `Alert`, `Label`, `Input`, `Field`, `PasswordInput`, `PasswordRequirements`, `HelperText` and `Button`.
platform/auth.guidelinesSummary: The signed-out screens of a platform app: sign in, sign up, reset password and check your inbox, frame included. The user has one job here, to get into their account, and one object on the page to do it with: a single card under the signed-out bar. Every step of the flow (`email`, `password`, `reset`, `sent`, `new-password`) swaps the contents of that card in place, and every answer the server gives, success included, lands in one `Alert` inside it. Auth never toasts.

platform/create/create-in-drawer.name: CreateInDrawer
platform/create/create-in-drawer.title: Templates/Platform/Create/CreateInDrawer
platform/create/create-in-drawer.summary: The right-side form drawer every item created or edited inside a resource opens, such as a domain, a record, an environment, a variable or a rule: a panel header with the title, a muted one-line description and the close button; a disabled-while-saving fieldset of `SettingsSection` bands, each a heading with a hint glyph over its stacked `Field` components; and one submit button in the footer that flags empty required fields only after it is pressed and shows its loading state while the save is in flight. Its state resets each time it opens, so the content stays in place while it closes. Add Domain opens from under Domains on the resource’s Settings tab, from a domain row menu to edit it, and from Add Environment in the resource environment menu. The Environment select lists every environment, says when choosing one connects it to the resource, and ends in a Create Environment option. Choosing Bring my own domain drops the free-domain addon and reveals the Certificate select, preselecting a certificate that already covers the address. Built from `SettingsSection`, `Drawer` and its parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Field` (with `InputGroup` and `RadioButton` choice cards), `Label` and `HelperText` around `Select`, `NumberInput`, `Input`, `Textarea`, `Link`, `Alert` and `Button`. The same drawer comes in three more shapes, each a variant: ItemRows, an Origins page inside a resource whose Add Origin drawer groups `Item` rows under section-titled flush `Card`s; NestedDrawer, an Add Rule drawer on a resource's Rules Engine whose Origin select creates the missing origin of that same resource in a second, medium drawer stacked above it and selects it back; and DeploymentSettings, the drawer that creates a Deployment Setting from a Build and deployment settings panel. The variants add `PageHeader`, `SettingRow`, the platform shell, `Card`, `Item` and `Switch`.
platform/create/create-in-drawer.guidelinesSummary: The right-side drawer that adds or edits something that only exists inside another resource: a domain, a DNS record, an environment, a variable, a rule. platform/create/deploy-drawer.name: DeployDrawer

platform/create/deploy-drawer.summary: The drawer a platform deploys from, opened by the outlined Deploy button on a service or a project. Every variant shares one Resources card: a row per resource with its Ready tag, the picked version and a Change version menu, and a Dependencies disclosure with the modules and integrations the service references. On a service the default flow is environment first: the Project card uses an existing project or creates one, the environments come as radio blocks, and Projects impacted lists every project the environment’s shared Deployment Settings publish to. A deploy started without a pinned version first builds one, so the drawer opens as Build and deployment with a Building row and the other sections faded. A service can also deploy project first, picking the project before the environment. On a project, the drawer carries every resource it serves and warns when its Deployment Settings also publish elsewhere. Built from `SettingsSection`, `Drawer`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Card`, `Item`, `Accordion`, `Separator`, `Popover`, `DropdownMenu`, `ToggleGroup`, `Field` choice cards with `RadioButton`, `Input`, `Avatar`, `Tag`, `Spinner`, `Alert`, `Tooltip` and `Button`.
platform/create/deploy-drawer.guidelinesSummary: The drawer a platform deploys from, opened by Deploy on a service or a project. The user is about to put a version into traffic and needs to confirm exactly what goes out (each resource and dependency at a version), where it goes (a project and one of its environments) and what else it reaches (every project that shares the environment's Deployment Settings). One Deploy at the foot commits all of it.

platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog.name: DeployProgressDialog
platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog.title: Templates/Platform/Create/DeployProgressDialog
platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog.summary: The modal progress of one deploy that activates several Deployment Settings, each on its own, and the drop-to-deploy confirm that starts it. The `Dialog` is titled Deploying 2 of 5… while it runs, cannot be dismissed and keeps Close disabled; under the title the tally says how many succeeded and failed and that the ones that succeeded stay live. A `Progress` bar and Activating <name> track the run, a `ToggleGroup` filters All, Deploying, Failed and Done with their counts, and each row names the settings and the environments and projects it reaches, with a `Spinner` and a status `Tag` while it deploys and an `OutcomeMark` once it settles. When the run settles the header gains a large `OutcomeMark` and the outcome reports through one toast with Edit and Redeploy, as every async action does; a failed row says why and the footer offers Retry failed. The toast stays the standard for deploys: this dialog is only for the drop-to-deploy and multi-settings path. Built from `Dialog`, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Progress`, `ToggleGroup`, `Spinner`, `Tag`, `OutcomeMark`, `Button` and `Toaster`.
platform/create/deploy-progress-dialog.guidelinesSummary: The modal progress of one deploy that activates several Deployment Settings, each on its own, and the drop-to-deploy confirm that starts it. The user dropped a folder (or started a deploy whose environment publishes through several Deployment Settings) and wants to see each one activate, know which failed and why, and retry only those. **The toast stays the standard.** Every deploy reports through one toast with Edit and Redeploy (`platform/states/async-submit`). This dialog is only for the drop-to-deploy path and for a deploy that fans out to several Deployment Settings; even there the outcome still reaches the user through the toast, so they can close the dialog and leave.

variants.name: Drop
variants.summary: The drop-to-deploy confirm: New production deployment, the service with a Production `Tag`, what the files replace, and the dropped folder with its file count, total size and a scrollable list of paths with sizes formatted by `Intl.NumberFormat`. Cancel closes; Deploy to Production opens the progress dialog and starts the run.

variants.name: PartialFailure

platform/create/deploy-success.name: DeploySuccess

Any create flow can end on it, with its own title and, when there is no Git source, no scope. Built from `SectionHeader`, `Card`, `Tag`, `Button`, `Tooltip`, `Item`, `ToggleGroup` and `CodeBlock`.
platform/create/deploy-success.guidelinesSummary: The screen a create flow ends on. The user has just watched a deploy finish and needs three answers before leaving: is it live and where, what exactly was created or bound along the way, and what to do next. The page answers them in that order in the terminal column of the wizard, then offers one way out to manage the resource.

variants.name: CliCreated

platform/create/deploy-template.name: DeployTemplate
platform/create/deploy-template.title: Templates/Platform/Create/DeployTemplate

The same column then shows the build and the outcome, so the user never leaves the page.

platform/create/deployment-flow.name: DeploymentFlow
platform/create/deployment-flow.title: Templates/Platform/Create/DeploymentFlow
platform/create/deployment-flow.summary: The deploy flow card a create flow streams while it deploys: a Card titled Deployment whose header carries the run status, a StatusIndicator while it runs and the Phased or Complete ToggleGroup once it has failed, opening on a cloning splash and then streaming the DeploymentLogs block with its controls moved up to that header: a Logs row with the step count, the pipeline as an Accordion of steps, each with its status glyph, its time and its own LogView, over a flush Progress. platform/create/deployment-flow.guidelinesSummary: The card a create flow hands its column to once the user has pressed Deploy. The card opens on a cloning splash, then streams the pipeline steps with their logs, and either hands over to the success screen or stays open on the failure.

platform/create/multipage-create.name: MultipageCreate
platform/create/multipage-create.title: Templates/Platform/Create/MultipageCreate
platform/create/multipage-create.summary: The page a first-level resource is created on one step at a time: the creation header, a Stepper rail on the left that unlocks each step once it is reached and shows the description of the current one, a form column that opens with the step heading, and a footer bar with Cancel on the left and Back plus Next on the right, Next turning into the create action on the last step. platform/create/multipage-create.guidelinesSummary: The page a first-level resource is created on one step at a time. The user first says where the resource runs, then answers each step's fields in order, and only reaches the create action on the last step. A rail on the left shows how far they are and lets them return to any step already reached; if the host they chose lacks a module the resource needs, a step is inserted that offers to turn it on, so nothing is created that would silently never be read.

platform/create/provision-wizard.name: ProvisionWizard
platform/create/provision-wizard.title: Templates/Platform/Create/ProvisionWizard
platform/create/provision-wizard.summary: A two-step creation wizard that provisions a resource and binds it to another: the creation header, a Stepper rail that only lets you go back, a page heading over the form column, and a borderless SaveBar footer that fades in over the canvas with Back and the primary action, Next and then Create and deploy. platform/create/provision-wizard.guidelinesSummary: The two-step wizard that provisions a resource bound to another and puts it into traffic. The user first binds the project the service serves, reusing one from a paged list or creating it right there with its cache and origin, then sets the domain traffic arrives on, the environment and certificate, and the deployment the first release is cut against. The address is previewed as they type, the defaults sit under Advanced, and the last button says it both creates and deploys, so the cost of pressing it is never a surprise.

platform/create/release-impact.name: ReleaseImpact
platform/create/release-impact.title: Templates/Platform/Create/ReleaseImpact
platform/create/release-impact.summary: The Review and deploy page of a release that carries several resources at once. The left column holds one card per resource: its type and icon, a Required or Read-only `Tag` or an include `Switch` named by a `Tooltip`, the resource and a version `Select` that tracks the latest Ready version or pins one (each with a Current `Tag` and its age), an invalid line and Build a version when nothing is Ready, and a Dependencies box whose `Accordion` groups modules and integrations with counts, a Shared `Tag` with the resources that also reference it and one info `Alert` saying a shared dependency deploys at one version. platform/create/release-impact.guidelinesSummary: The Review and deploy page of a release that carries several resources at once: a service, the policy in front of it, its storage, its error page and every dependency they reference. The user is about to put all of it into traffic and needs to see, before deploying, which version of each resource goes out, which dependencies go with it, and every Deployment Setting, environment and project the release reaches. One Deploy release at the foot commits it, after one confirmation.

platform/create/resource-picker.name: ResourcePicker
platform/create/resource-picker.title: Templates/Platform/Create/ResourcePicker
platform/create/resource-picker.summary: The card a create flow uses to bind one resource to another: a lead, a ToggleGroup choosing between an existing resource and a new one, then either a hint over a searchable list of the existing resources with a selected mark, paged five at a time with skeleton rows while the next page loads and a polite status line for screen readers, or a Name `Field` around an `Input` whose helper text carries the allowed characters and turns into the required message once Next is pressed empty. The user either reuses one of theirs or makes a new one on the spot, and answers it in one place: an Existing / New choice, then a searchable, paged list of what exists or the few fields that create a new one. platform/create/single-page-create.name: SinglePageCreate
platform/create/single-page-create.title: Templates/Platform/Create/SinglePageCreate
platform/create/single-page-create.summary: The page a first-level resource is created on in one screen: its own creation header with no sidebar, a centred form column opening with a small page heading, then stacked sections, each a heading with a Hint over a flush Card of field rows, and a fixed bar under the scrolling form, the same bar Version Detail uses, carrying an optional leading slot plus Cancel and the submit Button. The same page covers a resource with a General section and a collapsed Advanced section, and an action whose submit label follows what it does (Save, Purge, Create). A long create such as Create Service groups `Item` rows under small headings and ends in a full-bleed sticky footer. Fields flag required or invalid only after the submit Button is pressed, and each error clears as soon as its field is edited. Built from `PageHeader`, `SettingsSection`, `SettingRow`, `SaveBar`, `GlobalHeader`, `IconButton`, `Breadcrumb`, `Avatar`, `Card`, `Item`, `Input`, `HelperText`, `Switch`, `Field` choice cards with `RadioButton`, `Textarea`, `Alert`, `MultiSelect`, `NumberInput` and `Button`. ImportFromGit is the same job inside the platform shell with standalone `Field` stacks under plain headings instead of `Item` rows: the Git scope and repository side by side, Template settings, Deployment, Build and Runtime, Notifications and Alerts and Delivery features, ending with an acknowledgement checkbox and a single Deploy button at the end of the column, with no sticky footer; ImportFromGitSubmitted is that form after Deploy on the untouched fields.
platform/create/single-page-create.guidelinesSummary: The page a first-level resource is created on when everything it needs fits on one screen. The user arrives from the module's `Create <Object>` button, answers the required fields at the top, leaves the defaulted ones folded under Advanced, and commits from a bar that never scrolls away. The page has its own URL, its own creation header and no sidebar, so it survives a reload and the back button, and leaving it returns to the list.

platform/create/source-wizard.name: SourceWizard
platform/create/source-wizard.title: Templates/Platform/Create/SourceWizard
platform/create/source-wizard.summary: A creation wizard that starts a resource from a code source and deploys it: the creation header, a Stepper rail that only lets you go back, the form column, and a borderless fading SaveBar footer with Back and the primary action that disappears while a step is answered by a click. The source, repository, target and configure steps of each method, and the provisioning and success screens (DeploymentFlow and DeploySuccess), are not plotted here. Built from `PageHeader`, `GlobalHeader`, `Stepper`, `Field`, `Input`, `Button`, `SaveBar`, `Card` and `Item`.
platform/create/source-wizard.guidelinesSummary: The wizard that starts a resource from code and deploys it. The user first says which service the project deploys to (an existing one, a new one created inline, or none yet), then picks how the code arrives: import from Git, sync from the CLI or start from a template. The method they pick declares the steps that follow on the rail, and the flow ends on the provisioning log and the success screen. Steps answered by a click carry no Next, so the user moves as fast as they decide.

platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-das.name: ActivityOutcomesDashboard
platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-das.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/ActivityOutcomesDashboard
platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-das.summary: An activity outcomes dashboard: what a set of actors requested through the rules and what the rules decided. A page heading with a Refresh IconButton sits over a filter row of `Field`s (time range, actor, outcome and category Selects, and a destination Input that matches an exact host). A grid of seven StatTiles, four per row until the widest screens, counts the outcomes (requests, allowed, blocked, held, approved, denied and over budget), each with its delta against the previous period and a Hint that defines it. Below, a ChartCard plots outcomes over time as a Chart with stacked bars, one series per exclusive outcome in its status color (allowed success, blocked danger, held warning), with a legend that toggles a series and shows its total. Three ChartCards break the same requests down by actor, category and destination with a BarList each, and a last ChartCard holds the request log, a TableRoot with time, actor, an outcome Tag, category, a SeverityTag, destination, method and the rule that decided it. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`.
platform/dashboard/activity-outcomes-das.guidelinesSummary: The page an operator opens to answer "what did these actors ask for, and what did the rules decide?". It counts every request by its outcome (allowed, blocked, held, approved, denied, over budget), shows how those outcomes moved over time, breaks them down by actor, category and destination, and ends in the request log, where each row names the rule that decided it. Every region reads the same filters, so narrowing the time range or the actor moves the whole page at once.

variants.name: Loading
variants.summary: While the time range loads, the tiles, the chart and the breakdowns render their own Skeleton and the log holds Skeleton rows, so the page does not reflow when data arrives.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: A time range with no request. The tiles show a dash with no delta, the chart and the breakdowns keep their box with an empty state, and the log says what fills it and to widen the time range.

variants.name: Failed

platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard.name: AlertsDashboard
platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/AlertsDashboard
platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard.summary: An alerts dashboard: what is open, how severe it is, what kind it is and who is involved. A page heading with the period Select sits over four StatTiles (open, critical or high open, alerts in the period and the false positive rate), each with its delta and a Hint. Below, a ChartCard stacks the alerts raised each day by severity level, with every series colored from the severity ramp so the bars, the legend and the tooltip read the same scale as the tables. Beside it, Open by severity lists one SeverityTag per level with its open count and its share of the open alerts. A BarList ranks the alerts by type, the Highest risk table pairs each entity with its risk score and the SeverityTag of its worst open alert, and the Open alerts table leads every row with its SeverityTag, sortable from critical to info. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`.
platform/dashboard/alerts-dashboard.guidelinesSummary: The page a security or operations lead opens to triage: what is open, how severe it is, what kind of alert it is and which entities are involved. It leads with the open counts, shows how many alerts were raised each day by severity, and ends in the open alerts table, ordered from critical to info, where the reader picks what to work on next. Severity reads on one scale everywhere: tiles, chart, tags and tables.

variants.name: Failed

platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard.name: AnalyticsDashboard
platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/AnalyticsDashboard
platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard.summary: The analytics dashboard pattern: KPI tiles, charts and a table that all read the same period, so one change of range moves every region together. A row of four StatTiles (requests, data transferred, success rate and status 5xx, each with a sparkline and its change against the previous period) sits over a 12-column grid of ChartCards. Requests over time spans the grid as an area Chart, status codes as a multi-series line and requests by country as labeled horizontal bars share a row, and a searchable, paginated TableRoot of top hosts closes it. Every card carries the same header: title with a Hint, the aggregation and variation Tags, a Line or Bar ToggleGroup for time series, an Expand IconButton, and a DropdownMenu with Copy query and Export CSV. Built from `PageHeader`, `StatTile`, `ChartCard`, `Chart`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `Hint`, `ToggleGroup`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `DropdownMenu`, `Input` and `EmptyState`.
platform/dashboard/analytics-dashboard.guidelinesSummary: The page a developer or operator opens to see how much traffic their services handled and how well they handled it: requests, data transferred, success rate and server errors for the period, then the charts and the table that explain those totals. Every tile, chart and the table read the same period, so one change of range moves every region together. It is the reference grammar for the other dashboards: KPI row first, a 12-column grid of `ChartCard`s below, one shared card header.

variants.name: Loading

variants.name: Failed

Each product shows its own four StatTiles with sparkline and change against the previous period, over four ChartCards of area, line or stacked bar Charts that share one crosshair.

platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard.name: CompositionDashboard
platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/CompositionDashboard
platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard.summary: A composition dashboard: how a total breaks down into its parts and how that mix moved over time, here the organization’s monthly spend by category. Under a page heading with the period Select and an Export button sits a row of four StatTiles, the total first and then its three largest categories, each with the change against the previous month and a 12-month sparkline; a rise reads as bad, so every tile is `inverse`. Below, a 12-column grid of ChartCards: the stacked Chart of spend by category over 12 months (Area or Bar from a ToggleGroup, crosshair, one tooltip for every category, a legend with range totals) beside a DonutChart of the current month’s split with the total in its center, and a ranked contributors TableRoot across the full width: rank, the resource name behind its category glyph, the category Tag, the amount, its share of the total as a Progress with the percentage, and the change against last month as a Tag. Built from `PageHeader`, `StatTile`, `Chart`, `DonutChart`, `ChartCard`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `Progress`, `Hint`, `ToggleGroup`, `Select`, `DropdownMenu`, `IconButton`, `Button` and `EmptyState`.
platform/dashboard/composition-dashboard.guidelinesSummary: The page that answers "what is this total made of, and how did the mix move?". The block's example is the organization's monthly spend: the total and its three largest categories first, then the mix over 12 months, the current month's split, and the resources that drive it, ranked. The same shape fits any total that breaks down into exclusive parts (storage by type, requests by product, seats by team).

variants.name: Loading

platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboar.name: ConfigurableDashboard
platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboar.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/ConfigurableDashboard
platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboar.summary: A configurable dashboard: the reader arranges the cards. The page binds its layout, an array of id, span and height in order, to a Board with v-model:layout; an Edit layout Button turns on the board's editing, which shows the ChartCard drag handle and resize corner on every card. A card snaps to whole columns between 3 and 12 and to a height between 280 and 720 pixels; the board is twelve columns wide from a 48rem container and one column below it. Each card keeps its title with a Hint and nothing else in its header, and shows a Tag with its span while editing. Drop a card on another or press the arrow keys on its handle to move it; the board puts focus back on the moved handle and announces every move and resize in a polite live region. Reset layout appears once the layout differs from the default. Keep the layout wherever the product stores preferences. Built from `PageHeader`, `Button`, `Board`, `ChartCard` (with its drag handle and resize corner), `Hint`, `Tag`, `DonutChart`, `BarList` and `Chart`.
platform/dashboard/configurable-dashboar.guidelinesSummary: A dashboard the reader arranges: they move cards, change how many columns a card spans and how tall it is, and keep that layout. It serves readers who come back to the same page every day and care about different cards than the default puts first. The page owns the layout (an array of id, span and height, in order) and binds it to `Board`, which moves, resizes, clamps and announces; the `ChartCard` inside each `Board.Item` provides the drag handle and the resize corner.

variants.name: Editing
variants.summary: Edit mode. Drag a card by its handle onto another to swap their order, or drag its corner to change the span and the height. Focus the handle and use the arrow keys to move a card, or focus the corner and use Left and Right for the span, Up and Down for the height.

platform/dashboard/data-dashboard.name: DataDashboard
platform/dashboard/data-dashboard.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/DataDashboard

Six StatTiles carry each metric’s period total, a sparkline and the change against the previous 24 hours, each with a Hint that defines the metric. Under them, a ChartCard draws data transferred this period over the previous one as two series, a labeled horizontal bar Chart ranks the projects by data transferred, and a searchable, paginated TableRoot lists requests and data transferred per project. Every card keeps its Sum and change Tags, an Expand IconButton and a DropdownMenu with Copy query and Export CSV. platform/dashboard/data-dashboard.guidelinesSummary: The usage page: how much the account's projects consumed in the period, how that compares with the previous period, and which projects drove it. It leads with six KPI tiles (each with a sparkline and the change against the previous 24 hours), then explains the headline number with this period against the previous one, a ranking of projects and a table of usage per project.

platform/dashboard/executive-summary-das.name: ExecutiveSummaryDashboard
platform/dashboard/executive-summary-das.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/ExecutiveSummaryDashboard
platform/dashboard/executive-summary-das.summary: An executive summary dashboard: one page a lead reads to see how the quarter went. A page heading with the quarter Select and Export sits over a scorecard row of six StatTiles (revenue, monthly active users, net revenue retention, NPS, uptime and cost per request), each with its delta against last quarter and a Hint that defines it. Below, a trend grid of small multiples, one ChartCard per metric with a compact Chart (Area or Line) over the last 12 months and a Tag with the twelve-month change, shares one active index so hovering a month moves the crosshair on every card. A side column holds the goals, a Card of goal bars where each goal shows its label, a status Tag (On track, At risk, Off track), a Progress of current against target and both figures, and the commentary, a Card of Item rows with the author Avatar, role, date and the note itself. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`.
platform/dashboard/executive-summary-das.guidelinesSummary: The one page a lead reads to see how the quarter went: the headline results against last quarter, the twelve-month trend behind each one, progress on the quarter's goals and the notes the leads wrote when they reviewed it. It favours a few numbers read in seconds over detail; every figure links back to its own dashboard for the breakdown.

platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboa.name: FunnelCohortDashboard
platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboa.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/FunnelCohortDashboard
platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboa.summary: A funnel and cohort dashboard: how people move through the steps from a first visit to a paid plan, and how well each weekly sign-up cohort is retained. The page opens with a heading and one global filter bar, a period and a segment `Select`, so every region renders the same slice. Below it, a row of five `StatTile`s (visitors, sign-ups, activated, paid and overall conversion, each against the previous period with a sparkline) sits over a 12-column grid of `ChartCard`s. The conversion funnel spans the grid: a horizontal, labeled `Chart.Bar` of the steps beside a `TableRoot` that states each step’s users, its share of visitors and the drop-off from the step before. Cohort retention shares the next row: a multi-series `Chart.Line` of retention by week since sign-up, one series per weekly cohort, and a cohort `TableRoot` with each cohort’s size and its week 1 to week 6 retention in tabular figures, where a dash marks a week that has not ended. There is no heatmap: the retention matrix is a plain table, not colored cells. Each card header carries a title with a `Hint` and a menu with Export CSV. Built from `PageHeader`, `Select`, `StatTile`, `ChartCard`, `Chart`, `TableRoot`, `EmptyState`, `Hint`, `DropdownMenu`, `IconButton` and `Button`.
platform/dashboard/funnel-cohort-dashboa.guidelinesSummary: The growth page: how people move through the steps from a first visit to a paid plan, where they drop off, and how well each weekly sign-up cohort keeps coming back. One global filter bar (period and segment) drives every region, so the funnel, the tiles and the cohorts always describe the same slice of users.

platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboar.name: HealthScoreDashboard
platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboar.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/HealthScoreDashboard
platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboar.summary: A health score dashboard: how well something performs for the people who use it, read as one score out of 100 and its bands. A page heading with the period Select sits over the overall score, a ChartCard with the figure, its band Tag (Good at 80 or more, Fair from 50 to 79, Poor under 50), the top cause of poor samples and a Line Chart of the score per hour. Two ChartCards rank the score per application and per location in a BarList, lowest first, each row naming its top cause. An hourly score card gives every application a Tracker strip, one block per hour colored by band, with its current band Tag at the end of the row. Under the grid, a Card lists the open incidents as Item rows: what is affected, the cause, how many devices and what share of samples, when it opened, and its band. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`.
platform/dashboard/health-score-dashboar.guidelinesSummary: The page that answers "how well does this work for the people who use it, and where is it worst?". Experience is reduced to one score out of 100 with three bands (Good at 80 or more, Fair from 50 to 79, Poor under 50). The page shows the overall score and its trend, ranks applications and locations lowest first with the top cause of poor samples, gives each application an hour-by-hour strip, and ends in the open incidents that need someone's attention.

platform/dashboard/home-dashboard.name: HomeDashboard
platform/dashboard/home-dashboard.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/HomeDashboard
platform/dashboard/home-dashboard.summary: The whole Home page inside the platform shell, in both of its states. **Populated** (once the account owns a resource): a greeting heading, a usage band with four chartless StatTiles (each label explained in a Tooltip in the tile’s aside slot, each figure beside its unit and delta Tag) next to the dismissible agent onboarding card, and a five-column resources grid with the Projects, Resources, Domains and Recents panels, every row a full-width link with a hover-revealed actions DropdownMenu. **Empty** (a brand-new account): the first-access screen, a greeting under a centred headline, the command prompt that opens the shell’s palette on click or Enter, and the three doors (ship something new, add a domain with its availability check, onboard your agent). The first-access content on its own is the Onboarding template; while either screen arrives, the PageWires Overview and Onboarding wires hold the page. Built from `StatTile`, `Card`, `Tooltip`, `IconButton`, `Item`, `DropdownMenu`, `Input`, `Kbd`, `Popover`, `Spinner`, `Illustration`, `Button` and the agent marks from the webkit assets.
platform/dashboard/home-dashboard.guidelinesSummary: The Console's Home page inside the platform shell: the first screen a signed-in user lands on. Its job is to get them back to work fast. For an account that owns resources it shows a short usage band and the resources they touch most (projects, resources, domains, recents), every row a link. For a brand-new account it becomes the first-access screen: a greeting, the command prompt and three doors to a first project, a first domain and a coding agent. It is not an analytics page; detail lives on each resource's own dashboard.

platform/dashboard/project-status-dashbo.name: ProjectStatusDashboard
platform/dashboard/project-status-dashbo.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/ProjectStatusDashboard
platform/dashboard/project-status-dashbo.summary: A project status dashboard: where a project stands against its plan, for one project and sprint at a time. The page opens with a PageHeader whose actions hold two Selects (project and sprint), then a row of four StatTiles (completion, tasks done, open tasks and overdue, each against the previous sprint), over a 12-column grid of ChartCards. A DonutChart splits every task by status (done, in progress, not started, and blocked in the danger color) beside the sprint burndown, a Chart of two Lines (actual story points left against the ideal straight line to zero) tagged with how far behind the sprint runs. The milestone timeline and the at-risk list share the next row: the timeline is an Item list with the date, title and a StatusIndicator per checkpoint, since there is no timeline component; the at-risk list is Item rows with the reason and a Tag. The owners table closes the grid, a TableRoot with each owner’s Avatar and name, open and done counts, and overdue as a danger Tag. Every card carries the same header: title with a Hint, its tags, and a menu with Copy link and Export CSV. Built from `PageHeader`, `StatTile`, `ChartCard`, `DonutChart`, `Chart`, `Item`, `StatusIndicator`, `TableRoot`, `Avatar`, `Tag`, `Select`, `Hint`, `DropdownMenu`, `EmptyState`, `Skeleton` and `Button`.
platform/dashboard/project-status-dashbo.guidelinesSummary: Where one project stands against its plan, one project and sprint at a time. A lead or a team member opens it before a stand-up or a review to see completion, the sprint burndown, the next milestones, what is at risk and who carries the open work. The page heading (`Project status`) sits over a filter row that picks the project and the sprint; every region reads that pair.

platform/dashboard/scan-results-dashboar.name: ScanResultsDashboard
platform/dashboard/scan-results-dashboar.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/ScanResultsDashboard
platform/dashboard/scan-results-dashboar.summary: A scan results dashboard: items sent for analysis, the verdict each one received and what is still waiting. A page heading with a Refresh IconButton sits over a row of six StatTiles (submitted, in analysis, last 24 hours, flagged, held for a verdict and open alerts), each with a Hint that defines it. Below, three cards share a row: a DonutChart of the verdicts (Clean, Suspicious, Flagged and Pending, in their status hues) with the item count in its center, a BarList of the sources the items came from, and a Card that sums up the deliveries held for a verdict and the items delivered before they were flagged, each with a Link to its list. A Submissions card across the full width holds the filter row (an Input search and Selects for status, verdict and source) over a paginated TableRoot: name, the verdict Tag, category, score, type, size, source, first submitter and last seen. Built from `PageHeader`, `StatTile`, `DonutChart`, `BarList`, `ChartCard`, `Card`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `Link`, `Input`, `Select`, `Hint`, `IconButton`, `Skeleton` and `EmptyState`.
platform/dashboard/scan-results-dashboar.guidelinesSummary: The page for a pipeline that sends items (files, attachments, packages) for analysis and gives each a verdict. The reader checks what was submitted, what is still waiting, what was flagged, and above all two exceptions: deliveries held until a verdict arrives, and items that were delivered before they were flagged. It ends in the submissions table, where the reader finds a specific item.

platform/dashboard/security-dashboard.name: SecurityDashboard
platform/dashboard/security-dashboard.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/SecurityDashboard
platform/dashboard/security-dashboard.summary: The security dashboard pattern: blocked and allowed requests over time, breakdowns by attack category and origin, the top sources and an attention list. A row of three StatTiles (Requests blocked, Requests inspected, Block rate, each with its delta against the previous period and a sparkline) sits over a 12-column grid of ChartCards. Matched requests over time plots blocked and logged requests; Needs attention lists the settings and traffic that ask for a decision, each with a severity Tag and one action Link; attack categories and countries read as ranked BarLists, and the top source IPs as a searchable, paginated TableRoot. With no rule set in place the tiles stay as dashes and one setup EmptyState that offers Add rule set replaces the grid. Built from `PageHeader`, `StatTile`, `ChartCard`, `Chart`, `BarList`, `Item`, `Tag`, `Link`, `TableRoot`, `Hint`, `ToggleGroup`, `DropdownMenu`, `Skeleton`, `EmptyState` and `Button`.
platform/dashboard/security-dashboard.guidelinesSummary: The page a reader opens to see what their security rules are doing: how many requests were blocked and inspected, how blocking moved over time, which attack categories and countries it came from, which source addresses sent the most, and the short list of settings and traffic that need a decision now. Needs attention is what makes it more than a report: every entry ends in one action.

platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-da.name: ServiceMonitoringDashboard
platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-da.title: Templates/Platform/Dashboard/ServiceMonitoringDashboard
platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-da.summary: The service monitoring dashboard pattern: status tiles with sparklines, multi-series charts and an alert rail. One StatTile per service carries its p95 latency, the change against the previous period and a sparkline, with a StatusIndicator naming its state in words. Below, Latency (p50, p95, p99) and Error rate (Status 4xx, Status 5xx) sit in ChartCards as multi-series line Charts, each with its own window ToggleGroup, while an Open alerts rail holds the right edge: a fixed-width column that scrolls on its own, independent of the tiles and charts, listing each alert as an Item in an Item.Group with a severity Tag. Under the xl breakpoint the rail folds below the charts and the page scrolls as one. Built from `StatTile`, `StatusIndicator`, `ChartCard`, `Chart`, `ToggleGroup`, `Hint`, `Item`, `Tag`, `Skeleton` and `EmptyState`.
platform/dashboard/service-monitoring-da.guidelinesSummary: The page an on-call engineer keeps open: is every service up, how fast is it answering, how many requests fail, and which alerts are open right now. One tile per service states its p95 latency and its state in words; latency percentiles and error rates sit in two charts with their own window; the open alerts live in a rail on the right that scrolls on its own, so the alerts stay in view while the reader studies a chart.
