platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation.name: DeleteWithConfirmation
platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation.title: Templates/Platform/Delete/DeleteWithConfirmation
platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation.summary: The destructive confirmation a resource list uses for Delete: a warning `Alert`, a sentence naming what goes with the resource and a Help Center link, then a prompt that shows the resource name as a click-to-copy chip and an input the user must match before Delete enables. Every resource list, a folder of files and a table of records open it from the row Delete action; the title reads Delete plus the resource kind, and a container that holds other items passes its own consequence sentence. The typed confirmation and the Copied reveal reset each time the dialog opens, so the content stays put while it closes. Built from `ConfirmDialog` (the body in its default slot, Cancel and Delete in its `actions` slot), `Alert`, `Tooltip`, `Input` and `Button`; closed by default behind a visible danger trigger. The LabelledField variant asks for the name through a labelled `Field` + `Input` inside a medium `Dialog`, opened from an outlined `Item` row on the page, for a delete that sits in a settings form rather than a list.
platform/delete/delete-with-confirmation.guidelinesSummary: The last stop before a resource is gone for good. The user chose Delete from a row menu or a settings page and now has to see what goes with the resource, take one deliberate step to prove they mean this one, and either confirm or back out. The dialog makes the irreversible action slow on purpose: Delete stays disabled until the typed name matches.

variants.name: LabelledField

The field clears every time the dialog opens, so its content stays in place while it closes. It is the form counterpart of the default Delete dialog on the resource lists, which renders the name as a copy chip with a bare input instead of a labelled field. Built from `PageHeader`, the platform shell, `Item`, `Dialog` with its trigger, portal, overlay, content, title and close parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Alert`, `Field`, `Input` and `Button`.

platform/detail/attached-resources.name: AttachedResources
platform/detail/attached-resources.title: Templates/Platform/Detail/AttachedResources
platform/detail/attached-resources.summary: An attached-resources card in a resource settings tab, here its domains: a borderless data-driven table of the addresses the resource answers on, each with its environment as the row's one medium rounded tag, its deployment policy as text, its certificate as a verified glyph and text, and a row actions menu, over a footer that counts them and adds one. Rendered in the Domains section of a resource’s Settings tab, where an environment-less domain leaves its Environment and Policy cells empty and the count reads domain or domains. Built from `Card`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `DropdownMenuRoot`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip` and `Button`.
platform/detail/attached-resources.guidelinesSummary: A short list of the things one resource is attached to, shown in place inside its Settings tab. Here they are its domains: the user sees every address the resource answers on, which environment, deployment policy and certificate each one uses, and can edit, delete or add one without leaving the settings page.

platform/detail/deployment-logs.name: DeploymentLogs
platform/detail/deployment-logs.title: Templates/Platform/Detail/DeploymentLogs
platform/detail/deployment-logs.summary: The deploy logs block on its own: a Logs row that reports the step count and the step in flight while the run goes, or the outcome Tag, the time and the Phased or Complete switch once it has settled; then the pipeline as an Accordion of steps, each with its status glyph, its title and sentence, its time and its own LogView, or every line as one continuous LogView in the Complete view; and a flush Progress on the bottom edge while it runs. Inside a deploy flow card it moves its controls up to the card header; on a deployment detail page it sits inside a Deployment logs card without its Logs row and progress bar. Built from Accordion, LogView, Spinner, Tag, ToggleGroup and Progress.
platform/detail/deployment-logs.guidelinesSummary: The user started a deployment and wants to know where it is, whether it went live and, when it did not, exactly which step failed and why. This block shows the pipeline as ordered steps, each with its status, its one-line outcome, its time and its own log output, so the user can follow the run as it streams, then read the full output once it settles.

platform/detail/details-page.name: DetailsPage
platform/detail/details-page.title: Templates/Platform/Detail/DetailsPage

The resource overview follows it with Get started for a resource made from the CLI, and the same page plots its Versions tab (the versions table) and its Build tab (repository, build configuration and token bands); the service overview ends its breadcrumb on the environment picker and follows the summary with the production checklist and the deployment topology. The summary card on its own, in its resource, service and policy shapes, is the Resource, Service and Policy variants: a subject band with the primary link and the actions, a band of labelled facts, and a state band on the canvas fill. The deployment page sits in the same shell without tabs: a status banner, the Deployment details card with its Deployment Settings band, and the Deployment logs card whose header carries the duration or the status and the Phased or Complete switch over the DeploymentLogs steps. The version page of a resource is the VersionDetail template and the deploy drawers opened from these pages are the DeployDrawer template (Templates/Platform/Create/DeployDrawer). The Deployments tab of a resource and of a service is the TableView controls row over a deployments table, scoped to the resource (the resource tab adds a small Deployments heading with Documentation and an outlined Deploy action); the service Settings tab is a variant of Templates/Platform/Edit/EditResource. Built from `PageHeader`, `PageTabs`, `SectionHeader`, `SettingsSection`, `SettingRow`, `SaveBar`, the platform shell, `Select`, `Tabs`, `TableRoot`, `EmptyState`, `InputGroupRoot`, `Card`, `DropdownMenu`, `Popover`, `Accordion`, `Flow`, `Item`, `Drawer`, `Alert`, `LogView`, `CodeBlock` and `ToggleGroup`; the summary card variants add `Button`, `IconButton`, `Tag`, `StatusIndicator`, `Avatar`, `CopyButton` and `Tooltip`.
platform/detail/details-page.guidelinesSummary: The second-level page of one resource. The user arrives from a list row or a deploy flow to answer three questions about it: where it lives and whether it is serving, what it is made of, and what to do next. The page names the resource in the breadcrumb, splits its concerns into tabs, and opens the Overview tab on one summary card of facts, followed by whatever the resource needs next: Get started for a resource made from the CLI, the production checklist and topology for a service.

Built from `Card`, `Button`, `IconButton`, `DropdownMenu`, `Popover`, `Tag`, `StatusIndicator`, `Avatar`, `CopyButton`, `Accordion`, `Alert` and `Tooltip`.

variants.name: Policy

An empty field takes the `required` state, a filled but wrong one takes `invalid`, and its helper text swaps the guidance for the message, so each field speaks in one place and there is no summary. Submit moves focus to the first field in error. A rejected request that no field owns raises an error toast with Retry and keeps the entries. A rejection a field owns, a key already in use, lands on that field and in a danger `Alert` above the fields, and never toasts. A successful save raises a success toast and clears the form. One `Toaster` is mounted with the form. While the form loads, `Skeleton` rows stand in for the fields and Create is disabled. Every story is wired: press Create with API_TOKEN as the key to get the conflict, or any other valid key to get the success state. Below md the actions stack at full width. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`. A rejection the server scopes to one section of a long form (a linked resource deleted while the form is open) is the FormError template (Templates/Platform/States/FormError).
platform/states/form-validation.guidelinesSummary: Every state a submit can land in, on one create form. The user's job is to create a resource and, when something stops the save, to know exactly which control to touch and that nothing they typed was lost. The primary is a short Create Variable page (heading, four fields straight on the canvas, Cancel and Create); the variants walk it through validation, the in-flight lock, an unscoped failure, a conflict, success and loading. A server rejection scoped to one section of a long form is its own block, `platform/states/form-error`.

variants.name: ValidationErrors
variants.summary: Create pressed with gaps. The empty Value and Environment take the required state, the malformed key takes the invalid state, each helper text carries its own message, and focus moves to Key.

variants.name: Submitting
variants.summary: The request is in flight. Create shows its loading state, and the fields and Cancel are disabled so the entries cannot change mid-save.

variants.name: ServerError
variants.summary: The request failed and no field owns the failure. An error Toast says what failed and carries Retry, the lock is released, and every entry stays as typed.

variants.name: Conflict
variants.summary: The server rejected a value one field owns: the key is already in use. A danger Alert above the fields says so and that the entries are kept, Key takes the invalid state with its reason and the focus, and nothing toasts.

variants.name: Saved
variants.summary: The save went through. A success Toast names the new variable and where it is available, and the form is cleared for the next entry.

variants.name: Loading
variants.summary: The form while its data loads, such as the environments it offers or the record an edit form opens with. Skeleton rows hold the layout, and Create stays disabled until the fields arrive.

platform/states/not-found.name: NotFound
platform/states/not-found.title: Templates/Platform/States/NotFound
platform/states/not-found.summary: The page an app renders when it cannot show the address the user asked for. The primary is the 404: a full-height canvas centring an EmptyState whose figure is the large 404 numeral art, the title Page not found, one sentence that says the address leads nowhere, and two actions, Go to home (primary) and Docs (outlined, new tab). A visually hidden h1 names the error code the figure shows. Variants cover 403 (no access, with Switch account), 500 (a failure on the server, with Try again, System status and an error reference for support) and a resource that does not exist inside the console (bordered EmptyState in the content column with Back to the list). Built from `EmptyState`, `Button` and the `svg/error-404` and `svg/error-403` figures.
platform/states/not-found.guidelinesSummary: The page an app renders when it cannot show the address the user asked for: the address leads nowhere (404), the user may not see it (403), or the server failed to build it (500). The user's job is to understand, in one sentence, that the problem is the address or the access and not their work, and to get somewhere useful in one click. The block keeps the error code out of the headline (it is in the figure and in a hidden `h1`) and says what happened in plain words.

variants.name: Forbidden
variants.summary: 403: the address exists but the user's role does not include it. The 403 numeral art, You don't have access to this page, what to do (ask an admin, or switch account), and Go to home with Switch account.

variants.name: ServerError
variants.summary: 500: the page failed on the server. A warning icon tile in place of the numeral art, Something went wrong on our side, the reassurance that nothing saved was lost, Try again (which reloads and shows its loading state), System status in a new tab, and the error reference to quote to support.

variants.name: ResourceNotFound
variants.summary: Inside the console: the route is valid but the record is not (deleted, or a stale link). A bordered EmptyState in the content column names the resource and its ID, says why it may be missing, and offers Back to services.

platform/states/page-wires.name: PageWires
platform/states/page-wires.title: Templates/Platform/States/PageWires
platform/states/page-wires.summary: The skeleton wires an app paints while a page is still arriving: the Home overview (HomeWire), the first-access Home (HomeFirstUseWire), and the whole shell while an expired session signs out (SessionWire), which draws one of four bodies by the family of the page it covers: list, detail, create form or Home. Each one is the real page’s grid drawn with Skeleton bands inside the same Card frames, so nothing shifts when the content lands. In the app the session wire is a fixed full-viewport layer sized to the measured header and rail; here it fills the canvas at the header’s 56px and the rail’s `--container-2xs`. Built from Skeleton, Card and Item.
platform/states/page-wires.guidelinesSummary: The skeleton wires an app paints while a page is still arriving. The user's job does not change while they wait: they need to see the shape of the page they asked for, so the wire draws the real page's grid with `Skeleton` bands inside the same `Card` frames, and nothing shifts when the content lands. The set covers the Home overview, the first-access Home, and the whole shell while an expired session signs out, drawn over the family of page it covers (list, detail, create form or Home).

variants.name: Onboarding
variants.summary: The first-access Home wire: the headline and prompt bands over three door cards, each holding its illustration stage, three text lines and an action.

variants.name: Session
variants.summary: The whole app shell as a wire while a session expires over a list page: header bar, navigation rail with its grouped items, the list controls row and a table card with header, eight rows and pagination.

variants.name: SessionDetail
variants.summary: The same wire over a detail page: a strip of tab bands under the header, then a heading and two banded cards of field rows in the data column.

variants.name: SessionForm
variants.summary: The same wire over a create page: the heading and two banded cards of field rows in the create column, with the save bar held at the foot.

variants.name: SessionHome
variants.summary: The same wire over Home: the Overview wire centred in the data column.

platform/states/project-intake.name: ProjectIntake
platform/states/project-intake.title: Templates/Platform/States/ProjectIntake
platform/states/project-intake.summary: The surfaces a project passes through when it is dropped on the page: the dashed drop target that fills the page while a folder hovers over it, then the full-screen Initializing overlay that reads like the deploy logs: one row per received file as a step, its status glyph (a check once uploaded, a Spinner while it runs, a dashed ring while queued), the path and its size, advancing row by row, over the upload summary. A home page, its empty state, a creation hub and a project detail page render the drop target (the project page swaps the copy for “We build a new version of web-app, then you choose where it goes live.”); the home page, its empty state and the creation hub render Initializing over themselves. Built from `Card`, `Spinner`, Vue’s Transition and plain elements on theme tokens, with the step-row anatomy of the DeploymentLogs template.
platform/states/project-intake.guidelinesSummary: The surfaces a project passes through when the user drops it on the page. The user's job is to deploy a folder they already have without filling in a form: while a folder hovers over the page, a dashed drop target fills it and says what will happen; once it is dropped, a full-screen Initializing overlay reads like the deploy logs, one row per received file, until the upload is done and the deploy takes over.

variants.name: Initializing
variants.summary: The Initializing overlay mid-upload, held inside a layout-contained frame here so it does not cover the docs page: two files uploaded, the third running, two queued, each row a step with its status glyph, path and size.

platform/view/card-view.name: CardView
platform/view/card-view.title: Templates/Platform/View/CardView
platform/view/card-view.summary: The card form of a first-level list page, for resources people recognise by a few fields rather than compare column by column: a medium page heading with the resource name and its one-line description and the outlined medium Documentation action beside a primary large Create Application, the page's only large control, then the controls row: a `PropertyFilter` (Name, Status, Region, Requests, or free text) that grows to fill the row, a Delete button that counts the selected cards and opens a `ConfirmDialog` (the delete-with-confirmation pattern: a warning `Alert`, the selected names and an `Input` that must read delete), and `CollectionPreferences` for the page size and which fields every card shows; then `Cards` and a `Pagination`. Each card is named by a link to the resource and lists its fields as label and value pairs (the status as a `Tag`, the domain isolated in `bdi`, the request count in compact notation). Four cards a row in a wide container, down to one in a narrow one (container queries). A visible Select all items sits above the cards and the selection survives paging. All of it runs on `useCollection` in client mode: the filter, the sort and the page live in the URL, and the page size and the visible fields are saved per account in localStorage. An account with no applications keeps the heading and the controls and shows a medium `EmptyState` with a Create action; a filter that matches nothing shows a No matching applications state with Clear filters. Laid out with the theme’s `layout-boundary`, `layout-column` and `layout-section-start` utilities. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`.
platform/view/card-view.guidelinesSummary: The first-level index of one resource type, in cards. The user lands here from the sidebar to find a resource they recognise by its name and a few fields (its status, domain, region, traffic), narrow the list by those fields, open one, or select several and act on them together. One `useCollection` call holds the filter, the sort, the page, the selection across pages and the saved preferences, so the page is one heading over one band: the controls row, the cards and the pagination.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: An account with no applications: the heading and the controls stay, and the cards give way to a medium EmptyState with a small secondary Create Application button.

platform/view/file-browser.name: FileBrowser
platform/view/file-browser.title: Templates/Platform/View/FileBrowser
platform/view/file-browser.summary: The file browser a storage resource opens on: one flush `Card` holding a borderless `TableRoot` whose toolbar is the whole page header. The toolbar stacks the storage name beside the storage glyph, a large row of the table’s own search plus the refresh, download and columns IconButtons, then a `Breadcrumb` of the folder path beside the Add to files `SplitButton` (Upload file, Add folder). Folders sort first with a link-coloured folder glyph and open on click, a .. row leads back up once inside a folder, files take a glyph by extension, Size is muted and Last modified pairs the editor `Avatar` (named in a `Tooltip`) with the relative time; folders carry Open and files Download in their row menu, with Delete below, which opens a `ConfirmDialog` (a warning `Alert` and an `Input` that must match the name). Storage with nothing at its root renders the table’s empty slot: an `EmptyState` (This folder is empty) with a secondary Add to files split button; inside a folder the .. row always remains. Built from `Card`, `TableRoot` with `TableSearch`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `PopoverRoot`, `Switch`, `Breadcrumb`, `SplitButton`, `Avatar`, `DropdownMenuRoot` and `EmptyState`.
platform/view/file-browser.guidelinesSummary: The contents of one storage resource. The user opens a bucket to find a file, walk into a folder and back out, upload something or add a folder, and download or delete what is there. The table's toolbar is the whole page header, so the storage name, search, the folder path and Add to files all sit on the one surface the files live on.

variants.name: InsideAFolder
variants.summary: Inside a build folder: the crumb gains the folder, a .. row leads back up, and the files carry their glyph, size, editor and age.

platform/view/query-editor.name: QueryEditor
platform/view/query-editor.title: Templates/Platform/View/QueryEditor
platform/view/query-editor.summary: The query editor page placed in the platform shell: the Databases breadcrumb, then the Tables and Editor tabs, each pairing a resizable, collapsible `Sidebar` (288px at rest) with a working pane. On Editor the panel holds the query history and the pane stacks the Run query, Prettify and Templates toolbar, the editor, and the Results band over its pagination; on Tables the panel lists the tables and the pane holds the selected table with its Data and Definition switch. A database with no tables shows the Create Table empty state, and the Templates button opens the SQL quick templates drawer. Its page-level parts are `PageTabs`.
platform/view/query-editor.guidelinesSummary: The workspace of one SQL database. The user comes here to see which tables exist, read and edit a table's rows or its definition, and write and run queries against the data. Two tabs share one layout: a resizable side panel that lists things (tables, or past queries) beside a working pane that shows the one in use.

variants.name: Schema
variants.summary: The Definition view of customers: the Columns heading with Add column over a card holding the column name, its type as a Tag, and its constraints.

variants.name: EmptyDatabase
variants.summary: A database with no tables yet: the side panel says so and the working pane shows the Create Table empty state.

variants.name: Query
variants.summary: The Editor tab after the Select all query ran: the query history in the side panel, the statement in the editor, and its three rows in the Results band, switchable to JSON.

variants.name: Templates
variants.summary: The Editor tab before anything ran, with the Results band ready to execute; the Templates button opens the SQL quick templates drawer, and choosing a card loads its SQL into the editor.

variants.name: Failed
variants.summary: The rows of the selected table failed to load: the Tables tab keeps the side panel and the table toolbar, and the Data view shows a danger Alert that names the table and offers Retry.

platform/view/rules-list.name: RulesList
platform/view/rules-list.title: Templates/Platform/View/RulesList
platform/view/rules-list.summary: An ordered list of rules grouped by phase, the Rules tab of an application or a firewall. A `PageHeader` with Documentation and Add Rule sits over a search `Input` and a flush `Card` holding an `Accordion` with one item per phase (Request, Response), each trigger reading the phase and its rule count and each panel a composed `Table` with Order, Name, Description, Status and Last modified. The Order cell carries a position `Input` (type a number and press Enter), a grip `IconButton` that drags the row or moves it with the up and down arrow keys, and Move up and Move down `IconButton`s; every move is announced in a polite status region and focus follows the moved rule. A leading locked rule (the default rule) keeps first place and cannot be turned off; a search turns reordering off and says so in an info `Alert`. The Status cell is a `Switch` that turns a rule on or off without losing its place. Any change raises a `SaveBar` with Discard and Review changes; Review changes opens a `Dialog` listing, per phase, every rule that moves (from and to) and every rule turned on or off, with Cancel and Save, and a danger `Alert` in the dialog when the save fails. A success toast confirms the saved order. Built from `PageHeader`, `Button`, `Input`, `Alert`, `Card`, `Accordion`, `Table` and its parts, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `Tag`, `Switch`, `Skeleton`, `EmptyState`, `SaveBar`, `Dialog` and its parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter` and `Toaster`.
platform/view/rules-list.guidelinesSummary: An ordered list of rules grouped by phase: the Rules tab of an application (Request and Response phases) or a firewall (Request only). Order is behavior here, so the list is built to change the order safely: drag, keys or a typed position move a rule, every move is announced, and nothing runs in the new order until the user reviews the changes and saves.

variants.name: Firewall
variants.summary: A firewall's rules: one Request phase, five rules and no locked rule, so every rule moves; the page says rules run until one refuses the request.

variants.name: ReviewChanges
variants.summary: After two moves and one rule turned on: the SaveBar counts the changes and the Review changes dialog is open, listing Docs rewrite moving from 5 to 3 (and the rules it pushed down), Maintenance page turned on, and Security headers moving to the top of the Response phase.

variants.name: SaveFailed
variants.summary: The same changes after a failed save: the dialog stays open with a danger Alert saying the rules still run in the saved order, and Save reads Save again; the next attempt saves and closes the dialog with the success toast.

variants.name: Searching
variants.summary: A search for cache narrows both phases to their matches, the counts read n of total, an info Alert says reordering is off while searching, and every Order control is disabled with the reason in its name and tooltip.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: A firewall with no rules: the Request phase panel shows a small EmptyState with Add Rule instead of the table.

variants.name: Loading
variants.summary: While the rules load: both phases read Loading, the search is disabled, and each table shows three skeleton rows shaped like the columns.

platform/view/split-view.name: SplitView
platform/view/split-view.title: Templates/Platform/View/SplitView
platform/view/split-view.summary: The events explorer placed in the platform shell, with its navigation entry active: the controls row (Filter popover, event search, Refresh and Download CSV) over the applied filter chips, and the explorer. The explorer pairs a resizable, collapsible fields `Sidebar` (each field a column checkbox and a popover of its top values, grouped in an `Accordion` by category) with the log: the Events, Errors and Avg request time summary, the stacked volume chart whose buckets filter the period on click or drag, and the event `TableRoot`. Clicking a row opens the event document beside the log in a resizable end `Sidebar` when the explorer is wide enough, and in a `Drawer` when it is not.
platform/view/split-view.guidelinesSummary: The events explorer. The user comes here to answer what happened on their traffic: how many events, how many errors, when they spiked, and what one event looked like in full. They narrow the log by fields and time, scan the rows, and open one event beside the log without losing their place. The fields, the log and the event document are three panes of one workspace, and every filter acts on all of them at once.

variants.name: Filtered
variants.summary: Errors from the Security and Access Control sources: the Filter button counts three applied fields and each shows as a chip that reopens the popover on that field or removes it.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: A workspace with no traffic yet: the summary reads zero, the chart is flat and the log shows its No events yet state.

variants.name: Failed
variants.summary: The event log request failed: the fields panel stays, and the log pane shows a danger Alert that says the events did not load and offers Retry.

variants.name: Query
variants.summary: The Console Kit query bar on the sample design: a `DateRangePicker` (relative ranges, an absolute range typed in the chosen time zone, Previous and Next) drives the period, and `PropertyFilter` in query mode takes `level = Error AND host = api.example.com`, suggests fields, operators and values at the caret, explains an invalid query under the field and applies it on Enter. Saved queries (name, apply, delete) and Recent queries sit in two popovers beside the bar; the field values in the fields panel add or remove clauses of the query; the log, chart and times follow the chosen zone.

variants.name: Sessions
variants.summary: Several investigations open as tabs above the explorer, each keeping its own filters, search and period: API errors is active, with All traffic and Security blocks beside it. New investigation adds a tab (up to five, then a message says to close one); the actions menu renames (also F2 or a double click, with an inline field: Enter keeps, Escape cancels), duplicates or closes the active one (also Delete on the focused tab).

variants.name: EventDocument
variants.summary: An error event selected with its document open beside the log. The document lists every field of the event with a Search in this event field that narrows and highlights the fields, a Filter by and an Exclude button per value that apply to the log (an exclusion shows as an is not chip), and Copy that copies the fields shown as JSON; the full JSON document follows.

platform/view/table-view.name: TableView
platform/view/table-view.title: Templates/Platform/View/TableView
platform/view/table-view.summary: The canonical first-level list page: a medium page heading with the resource name and its one-line description, the outlined medium Documentation action and a primary large Create Resource, the page's only large control (on a phone they stack below the copy, each at full width), then the controls row and the resource table, laid out with the console page column and section rhythm. The whole list runs on `useCollection` in client mode: a `PropertyFilter` grows to fill the controls row and turns Name, Author, Status, Domain or free text into removable tokens (Match all or Match any, Clear filters, the match count), the sortable headers sort, the footer pages, and the filter, the sort and the page live in the URL so a filtered list can be shared. Beside the filter sit Refresh (the table’s loading state), Download CSV (every matching row) and `CollectionPreferences`, a dialog for the page size, the columns (shown, hidden and ordered; Name always shows), wrapped lines, striped rows and density, saved in localStorage. Any resource index takes this shape with its own columns and properties. The row menu's Delete opens a `ConfirmDialog` (the delete-with-confirmation pattern: a warning `Alert` and an `Input` that must match the resource name). A filter that matches nothing shows a No matching resources `EmptyState` with Clear filters inside the table; when the account has no resources left, the page keeps its heading and the controls row, and the table, without its header and footer, gives way to a flush `Card` holding only a medium `EmptyState` (the resource glyph, then a small secondary Create Resource and a small outlined Documentation on one row), so the list survives its last row being deleted. Laid out with the theme’s `layout-boundary`, `layout-column` and `layout-section-start` utilities carrying the inset, the measure and the vertical rhythm. Its page-level parts are `PageHeader`.
platform/view/table-view.guidelinesSummary: The first-level index of one resource type, in rows. The user lands here from the sidebar to find a resource among many, narrow the list by its attributes, compare records column by column, and act on one: open it, deploy it, clone it, delete it, or create a new one. One `useCollection` call holds the filter, the sort, the page and the saved preferences, so the page is one heading over one band: the controls row and the table it narrows.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: Every resource deleted on an account that is not new: `useCollection` reports `empty` (not `no-match`), so the page keeps its heading and controls, and the table, without its header or footer, gives way to a flush Card that holds only a medium EmptyState led by the resource glyph, with a small secondary Create Resource and a small outlined Documentation button.

platform/view/waf-tuning.name: WafTuning
platform/view/waf-tuning.title: Templates/Platform/View/WafTuning
platform/view/waf-tuning.summary: The Tuning tab of a WAF rule set: the requests it matched, grouped by rule, so the user can allow the legitimate ones. A `PageHeader` with Export to CSV and an allow action that reads Allow n selected once rows are checked; threshold settings above the table (a Time range `Select`, a Minimum hits `Input` that validates as a whole number, a search `Input` and a Refresh `IconButton`); and a flush `Card` with a data-driven `TableRoot` with row selection and sorting (Rule ID, Threat, Hits sorted high to low, and the top IP addresses, countries and paths, two shown and a `Tag` counting the rest). Rows below the minimum hits drop out, and a table with none left shows a small `EmptyState` saying how to widen it. Allowing opens a `Dialog` form listing the selected rules and how many allowed rules will be created (one per rule and path), with a required Reason `Textarea` whose error shows only after Allow rules is pressed; success closes it, clears the selection and raises a success toast, failure keeps it open with a danger `Alert` and Try again. Built from `PageHeader`, `Button`, `Field`, `Select`, `Input`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `Card`, `TableRoot`, `Tag`, `EmptyState`, `Dialog` and its parts, `PanelHeader`, `PanelContent`, `PanelFooter`, `Alert`, `Textarea` and `Toaster`.
platform/view/waf-tuning.guidelinesSummary: The Tuning tab of a WAF rule set. It shows the requests the rule set matched, grouped by the rule that matched them, with enough context (hits, top addresses, countries and paths) for the user to tell an attack from a false positive, and turns the legitimate ones into allowed rules with a recorded reason.

variants.name: Allow
variants.summary: Two rules checked and the Allow 2 rules dialog open: rule 1005 (SQL injection on 3 paths) and 1201 (Cross-site scripting on 3 paths), 6 allowed rules in all, and an empty Reason.

variants.name: AllowFailed
variants.summary: The same dialog after the allowed rules could not be created: a danger Alert says nothing changed in the rule set, and the submit button reads Try again.

variants.name: Empty
variants.summary: A rule set that has not matched any request: no threshold settings, and an EmptyState saying matches appear as traffic arrives.

variants.name: Loading
variants.summary: While the matches load: the settings and actions are disabled and the table shows skeleton rows.

shells/console.name: Console
shells/console.title: Templates/Shells/Console
shells/console.summary: The application shell every signed-in page renders inside: a full-height navigation rail on the left that the user resizes by its edge and collapses from its foot (the product wordmark, the ⌘K palette with its Recents, navigation, Actions and Account groups, the navigation Menu with its grouped sections and drill-in levels, and the account menu with the theme switch, the Upgrade to Pro action and the system status at its foot) and a content zone on the right whose global header carries the breadcrumb on every level (one unlinked crumb on a first-level list, which opens on its controls row with no page heading), the search affordance, the Create button, the Agent button and the account avatar. The search is a 32px field-shaped button while the bar’s content box is at least `--container-2xl` (752px) wide and an outlined IconButton below it; below `md` the rail becomes a Drawer opened from the hamburger that leads the wordmark. First-level lists, detail pages with their tabs and Home all render inside it. Built from `PageTabs`, `Sidebar`, `Menu`, `Command`, `DropdownMenu`, `ThemeSwitcher`, `StatusIndicator`, `Avatar`, `GlobalHeader`, `Breadcrumb`, `Button`, `ButtonHighlight`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `Kbd`, `Drawer` and, per page, `Tabs`, `Select`, `Tag`, `Input` and `Card`; the page bodies here are stand-ins, the real ones are the TableView and DetailsPage templates.
shells/console.guidelinesSummary: The application shell every signed-in page renders inside. The user browses and moves laterally between modules, so the shell keeps the whole product one step away: a navigation rail on the left (wordmark, the ⌘K palette, the grouped navigation, the account menu) and a content zone on the right headed by one global header (search, Create, Agent, the avatar). Pages render only their own content in the zone; this block's page bodies are stand-ins for `platform/view/table-view` and `platform/detail/details-page`.

variants.name: DetailPage
variants.summary: A resource detail page: the breadcrumb reads Resources, the resource, then its environment, whose last crumb is a Select that searches the resource’s environments, tags each with its deployment policy and offers Add Environment at its foot; a full-bleed Tabs bar under the header carries the Overview, Deployments and Settings tabs with the outlined Deploy action, and the content scrolls beneath it.

variants.name: Notifications
variants.summary: The same ListPage frame built on `AppLayout`: the bell in the header carries an unread `Badge` and opens the notifications region on the right (the tools region of the layout, a Drawer on a narrow screen), which lists deploys, invitations and alerts with Mark all as read and Clear all, and offers Edit and Redeploy on each deploy; a failed deploy also shows as a flash `Alert` above the page in the layout's notifications slot, and an empty list reads You are all caught up.

shells/documentation.name: Documentation
shells/documentation.title: Templates/Shells/Documentation
shells/documentation.summary: The documentation shell: a `GlobalHeader` in its `content` placement (see Templates › Headers › DocsHeader), a `Sidebar` rail from `lg` carrying a `MenuRoot` of the current product’s pages and the theme switcher in its footer, the reading column scrolling inside its own `ScrollArea`, and the “On this page” outline from `xl`. The `Footer` sits INSIDE the reading column’s scroller, in its `content` placement: the bands run full bleed across the zone between the rail and the outline and open on the page boundary, like the top bar above. Below `lg` the rail leaves and the footer takes the whole width; below `md` the footer stacks. The social buttons are small and row two sizes its bands by content, so the brand mark, seven icons and the status pair share one line in a zone as narrow as this column at 1024 wide; the brand leads that row from `lg` (answered by the `lg:` utility, so it follows the breakpoint token) and moves to the signature band below it. Built from `GlobalHeader`, `Sidebar`, `MenuRoot`, `ScrollArea`, `ThemeSwitcher` and `Footer`.
shells/documentation.guidelinesSummary: The documentation shell. A reader comes to learn one task and leave, so the shell keeps the page readable and the next page close: the docs header on top, a rail of the current product's pages from `lg`, a reading column that scrolls on its own, the "On this page" outline from `xl`, and the footer inside the reading column's scroller so the bands sit between the rail and the outline.

shells/website.name: Website
shells/website.title: Templates/Shells/Website
shells/website.summary: The website shell: a sticky `GlobalHeader` in its `site` placement (see Templates › Headers › SiteHeader), one `Hero` band opening the page, every section stacked inside one framed `SectionContainer max-width="site"` separated by hatched gaps, a closing frame that draws no rule of its own, and the `Footer` in its `site` placement closing the page frame. The hero, the sections and the footer all resolve to the site measure, which is the only reason the side rules running down the page are continuous; the hairline above the footer is the mirror of the hero’s top rule, so the frame turns the corner instead of stopping at it. The footer’s social buttons are small, the brand mark leads the social row from `lg` (answered by the `lg:` utility, so it follows the breakpoint token) and moves to the signature band below it, and row two sizes its bands by content, so the row never wraps while the status pair still has room. Built from `GlobalHeader`, `Hero`, `SectionContainer`, `SectionGap`, `SectionModule`, `FrameBox`, `BigNumbers`, `TextureMaterial` and `Footer`. The full mega-menus and the navigation sheet are documented on Templates › Marketing › Shell › SiteNav.
shells/website.guidelinesSummary: The marketing shell. A visitor scans to decide whether Azion fits, so the page is one continuous frame: a sticky site header, a hero band that states the offer and the two next steps, every section stacked inside one framed container separated by hatched gaps, and the site footer closing the frame. The hero, sections and footer all resolve to the site measure, which is what keeps the side rules continuous down the page.
